tower.papers.stuckVehicle: Cannot be taken on a shift until a renewal is recorded here.
tower.papers.onShiftWith: On a shift right now with {name}.
tower.papers.licenceBody: Record it as you have seen it. The day it is saved the courier can start a shift again; there is nothing else to clear. The courier’s own word is not enough — that is what the date is there to replace.
tower.papers.licenceDone: Licence recorded for {name} — the new date counts from now.
tower.papers.vehicleBody: The reference and the expiry date on each paper. The day after a date passes the vehicle is off the road until the renewal is recorded here; a paper with no date switches nothing off, and nothing watches it either.
tower.papers.vehicleDone: Papers recorded for {plate} — the dates are watched from now on.
tower.papers.cardsWaiting: {n, plural, one {# card} other {# cards}} to check
tower.papers.cardRead: Sent {date}. They read the expiry as {expires}.
tower.papers.cardOpen: Open the photo at full size
tower.papers.cardGone: This photo cannot be produced. Refuse it and say so — they can send it again.
tower.papers.readDate: Expiry date, as you read it on the card
tower.papers.differs: That is not the date they read ({expires}). Look at the card again before recording it.
tower.papers.refuseWhy: Why not — they are shown exactly this
tower.papers.lastRefused: Their last card was not accepted: “{reason}” — {who}, {date}.
tower.papers.nothingSent: Nothing sent. They send the renewed card from the driver app, which asks for it once the licence is running out.
tower.papers.checkedDeleted: Their ID and licence were checked by {who} on {date}, and the photos were deleted then. The number, the classes and the date are what was kept.
tower.papers.vetted: The licence they were vetted on — it shows the date at vetting, not a renewal
tower.papers.noDateWatched: No date on record, so nothing is watched and nothing switches off.
tower.papers.withoutPhoto: Record a date without a photo
tower.papers.contactNone: No contact details are held for this courier.
tower.papers.contactFailed: Could not read their contact details
tower.papers.contactReceipt: This look is recorded against your account.
tower.papers.readFromPhoto: The card this date was read from
tower.papers.daysLeft: {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} left
tower.papers.lapsedAgo: Lapsed {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} ago
tower.depots.f.notePh: Gate open 6am to 6pm, reach stacker on site
tower.imports.chainOneLeg: Only one road leg can be minted here today. Mint the one you need now and say which it is in the description; the second is tracked work.
tower.settings.title: Settings
tower.settings.lede: What you publish about yourself, the places you use, and how you sign in.
tower.settings.companyOnly: Network staff act for no company, so there is nothing here to set.
tower.settings.placesLede: Ports you collect from and addresses you deliver to. Add one while minting a road leg.
tower.settings.recordSub: What we hold and have verified about you.
tower.settings.pageSub: The page anybody can read about you.
tower.market.title: What the market is doing
tower.market.lede: What shippers asked for, against what the fleet actually took — day by day, how long loads are waiting, what negotiated prices cleared at, and which lanes went quiet.
tower.market.caveat: Every figure here is derived from timestamps a load already carries. A fleet withdrawing capacity files no notice — it simply stops claiming — so these lines move on their own within a day, which is the only reason they can be trusted in a market where people are busy and forms go unfilled.
tower.movers.title: Who moves loads
tower.movers.lede: The same record their public page carries, with two things it does not: why each load was handed back, and which driver handed it. Ordered by how busy they are — never by how well they did.
tower.movers.noneTitle: No fleet has taken a load yet
tower.movers.noneBody: A record appears here the first time somebody claims work off the board.
tower.movers.handBacksWhy: Not on their public page, and deliberately. A driver whose rest was due has done the right thing by handing a load back — publishing the reason would punish the honest use of a rule we wrote, and the answer to that is drivers who drive tired instead. The COUNT is public; the reason is for whoever is handling a complaint.
tower.movers.noHandBacks: They have never handed a load back.
tower.movers.perDriverWhy: Names appear here and nowhere public. A driver identifiable as the one who gave a load back is a driver who stops taking the difficult ones.
tower.movers.noDriverWork: None of their drivers has taken a load yet.
tower.market.thinWindow: Too few loads in this window to read a trend from. The counts are real; the shape of them is not worth much yet.
tower.market.movedHint: A different count: loads taken during this window, whenever they were posted. Not one of the three above.
tower.market.loadsKm: {loads, plural, one {# load} other {# loads}} · {km} km
tower.market.withdrawnBody: {n, plural, one {# load} other {# loads}} the shipper pulled back. Counted here and kept out of “nobody took”, because a load nobody was asked to carry is not the fleet falling short.
tower.market.deadheadBody: {km} km run empty to reach that work. Beside the moved figure, never inside it.
tower.market.waitHint: Measured on loads that were taken, against the same length of time immediately before. When trucks get scarce, loads still get posted and still get taken — they just wait longer first, and that shows here before it shows anywhere else.
tower.market.waitNow: {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}} to be taken, typically
tower.market.waitPrior: Before that: {hours, plural, one {# hour} other {# hours}}
tower.market.waitCount: from {n, plural, one {# load} other {# loads}}
tower.market.waitNone: Nothing was taken in this window.
tower.market.priceHint: Only loads whose price was NEGOTIATED can answer this. A load taken at the computed price IS the rate card, so counting those would drag every figure back towards it and bury the signal.
tower.market.priceNone: No negotiated loads in this window, so there is nothing to compare.
tower.market.priceThin: Too few negotiated loads to say what the market paid — {n} in this window, so one unusual deal would be the entire figure.
tower.market.daysLegend: tall bar posted · short bar taken
tower.market.daysAria: Posted and taken loads across {n, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
tower.market.laneThin: Too few loads either side to call it a rise or a fall.
tower.market.whoFailed: That did not load. Network staff and company administrators can see this; nobody else can.
tower.market.whoLoads: {n, plural, one {# load} other {# loads}} on this lane
tower.market.whoUnattributed: {n, plural, one {# load was} other {# loads were}} claimed with no vehicle recorded against them.
tower.market.whoNoneTaken: Nothing on this lane has been taken yet.
tower.market.lanesFoot: A lane is named from its two ends. An end too far from anywhere we know is “unknown” rather than snapped to the nearest big town.
tower.market.quietCount: {n, plural, one {# lane} other {# lanes}} went quiet
tower.market.mapLabel: The lanes on this page, drawn between their two ends
tower.market.mapBasis: Each line joins the two ends of a lane — it is not the road between them, and the dots are town centres, so two lanes inside one neighbourhood share a dot.
tower.market.notOnMap: One end is not a place we can name — not on the map
tower.market.unplaceable: {n, plural, one {# lane has} other {# lanes have}} an end we cannot place, so a radius cannot judge them.
tower.market.fold.priceNone: No negotiated loads in this window
tower.market.fold.priceThin: Too few to say — {n, plural, one {# negotiated load} other {# negotiated loads}}
tower.market.fold.daysNone: Nothing posted in the last seven days
tower.imports.needReason: Say why you are sending it back.
tower.borders.title: Crossing a border
tower.borders.lede: The rules of carrying goods from one country into another: where a border may be crossed and when, the permits and regional insurance a vehicle must carry, the size a crossing allows — and whether a foreign vehicle may carry loads inside the country at all.
tower.borders.caveat: A foreign vehicle is never offered a load inside a country unless a rule here says it may. Rules go one direction at a time: Kenyan trucks entering Tanzania are not Tanzanian trucks entering Kenya.
tower.borders.none: No rules yet — so no vehicle may carry loads inside a country it is not registered in.
tower.borders.waits.title: How long each post takes
tower.borders.waits.hint: From the loads whose drivers said they reached a post and cleared it, in the last 90 days
tower.borders.waits.none: No load has cleared a post yet. Until enough have, every crossing is promised our standard figure.
tower.borders.waits.median: about {hours} — the middle of {n} crossings; the longest {longest}
tower.borders.waits.notYet: our standard figure — not enough crossings yet
tower.borders.f.crossings: Crossings — one per line: name | hours
tower.borders.saved: Rule saved — dispatch asks it at every offer from now on.
tower.borders.needFrom: Which country do the vehicles come from?
tower.borders.sameCountry: A border is between two different countries.
tower.borders.badWeight: A weight limit is a number above zero.
tower.record.title: The record
tower.record.whole: {n} fingerprints kept · the chain is whole
tower.record.noLedger: No record of fingerprints on this server
tower.record.wholeSub: Every one follows the one before it and matches what it holds · first {first}, latest {last}
tower.record.brokenSub: At block {block}: {reason}. Every fingerprint after it cannot be relied on until this is understood: tell whoever runs the server.
tower.record.oneWriter: One server writes the store: process {pid}
tower.record.oneWriterSub: Since {since}. A second server against the same records refuses to start, and one that loses the lock stops.
tower.record.notKept: Nothing is kept on this server
tower.record.notKeptSub: Records live only while it runs (a test, or GLOS_PERSIST=off).
tower.pilot.title: The pilot, week by week
tower.pilot.lede: The four numbers the compendium judges the pilot on, each week against its target. A week that has ended is frozen and never counted again; this week is so far. Weeks run Sunday to Saturday, UTC.
tower.pilot.handshakeSub: {handed} scanned onto a bus · {missed} left behind
tower.pilot.takeInSub: median of {n} timed · slowest one in ten {p90}
tower.pilot.how.handshake: Handshake: of the parcels due onto a bus at a counter handover, the share the shop scanned onto it. One left behind counts against it, whatever the reason. Target {target}; below {warn} needs a name on it.
tower.pilot.how.loss: Lost or damaged: parcels declared lost that week and not found by the time it was frozen, and problems reported on parcels that week, per parcel taken in that week. Target under {target}; above {warn} needs a name on it.
tower.pilot.how.takeIn: Take-in time: the middle of the times the shops’ app measured, from the first touch on the take-in to the parcel taken in. Longer than 15 minutes was interrupted, not slow, and is not counted. Target under {target} s; above {warn} s needs a name on it.
tower.pilot.how.retention: Original shops working: of the shops that worked a counter in the pilot’s first week, the share that worked one this week. Judged from week {week}, against {target}.
tower.pilot.how.frozen: Handovers and take-in times are counted from 18 October 2026, when they began to be kept; weeks before show no number for them.
tower.reports.title: Damage claim reports
tower.reports.lede: Every problem reported, newest first. Staff decide nothing here: the report was made the moment the problem was reported, from the record as it stood, and whoever it is for hands it to their own insurer.
tower.reports.caveat: Conversations are never edited or deleted, so they can be shown if two people disagree. Act on the person, not the message: a pattern across several reporters is what matters.
tower.reports.emptyBody: A report appears here the moment somebody reports one, at a counter or from their app.
tower.reports.disputeLede: A party chose these messages and shared them. The copy is fixed and fingerprinted, so it cannot change after it was shared. The other side was told in the conversation.
tower.reports.disputeEmpty: No dispute reports have been shared.
tower.rates.title: What each sister charges
tower.rates.lede: Every sister prices for itself, per kind of work. The three layers are added, never compounded, and each one can be set for one lane or for everything.
tower.rates.caveat: A buyer sees a price; a merchant sees one platform fee line; nobody outside this screen sees it broken into three. It is separated so somebody can answer whether we are earning because the market is good or because we are carrying risk nobody is paying for — a question one blended percentage cannot be asked.
tower.pick.search: Search companies — name, country or currency
tower.rates.groupBody: It is the merchant of record nowhere and is never a party to a customer transaction, so it has no rates to set. It earns its licence fee from the sisters instead. Shown rather than hidden, so looking for its rates gives you an answer.
tower.rates.partnerBody: Where its country is set to Local partner, it pays the shops, hubs and drivers who work under its promise, at the figures below, in its own money. SeeBuyGet only keeps the record of what it owes them: no money of ours moves, so nothing else on this screen applies to it.
tower.rates.saved: Saved — {lane}. Nothing already sold is repriced.
tower.rates.stackHint: They ADD UP — they do not compound. Cost of risk is what carrying the exposure costs us; profit on risk is what we earn for choosing to carry it; margin is the general company layer.
tower.rates.emptyInherits: An empty box INHERITS — a lane falls back to this company’s own rate, and that falls back to the network default. The grey number in an empty box is what it would inherit. Clearing a box is how you give a number back.
tower.rates.sumOverCeiling: Those come to {sum}, over the {max} ceiling. They ADD UP — they do not compound.
tower.tax.title: Tax
tower.tax.hint: Money this company never owns for a moment: it is held, and it is handed over. Charged on the whole price including our own fee, because what is taxed is the sale and not the profit.
tower.tax.label: What it is called
tower.tax.registrationHint: This company’s number, not this lane’s. Every tax save carries it, so a rate and the authority to charge it stay one act.
tower.tax.needsRegistration: A rate above zero needs a registration number — charging tax you are not registered to collect is money taken in the name of an authority that has never heard of you.
tower.cover.title: Cover
tower.cover.hint: What is carried for free on everything, and what it costs to declare more. Charged on the value of somebody’s goods, which is a different base from the layers above — and it accrues to the claims provision rather than to revenue.
tower.cover.negative: A free cover limit cannot be negative.
tower.amounts.title: What a parcel costs, what each step pays, and what the road starts from
tower.amounts.noneOwn: All at the figures every company starts from
tower.amounts.hint: In {currency}. An empty box stands at the figure shown greyed in it, which is what every company starts from; type 0 for a step this company pays nothing for. A change counts for every step done from then on. It does not re-price what has happened: a parcel is refunded what it was charged, and a parcel already past its free time keeps the daily rate it started at.
tower.amounts.k.wholesale: A parcel taken in at the counter
tower.amounts.h.wholesale: Charged to the shop’s float. It is also the float a shop needs to take the next one in, and its credit line is counted in parcels at this price.
tower.amounts.k.labourFee: Taking in a parcel that is already paid for
tower.amounts.h.labourFee: Paid to the shop — or the shop’s own fee, where that is more.
tower.amounts.k.handoverFee: Handing a batch to the driver
tower.amounts.h.handoverFee: Paid to the shop, once for each batch.
tower.amounts.h.toteLoadFee: Paid to the driver who scans it aboard, on top of what the road pays.
tower.amounts.k.mdpPassOnFee: A new hub’s fee for a bag passed on
tower.amounts.h.mdpPassOnFee: What a hub is paid for a whole bag it receives on its seal and passes on unopened, where it starts. Each hub then sets its own.
tower.amounts.h.mdpSortFee: Where a hub starts. Each hub then sets its own fee, and is paid that for each parcel it sorts.
tower.amounts.k.shelvingFee: Shelving a parcel that has arrived
tower.amounts.h.shelvingFee: Paid to the receiving shop when the parcel lands on its shelf — or the shop’s own fee, where that is more.
tower.amounts.k.releaseFee: Handing a parcel to its receiver
tower.amounts.h.releaseFee: Paid to the receiving shop when it is collected — what of it the shop’s own fee did not already pay at shelving.
tower.amounts.k.holdingFeePerDay: Holding a parcel, for each day
tower.amounts.h.holdingFeePerDay: Owed once the free collection time has ended, and never more than the journey cost.
tower.amounts.roadHint: A vehicle registered in this country starts from these where its owner names no rate of their own, and its owner can change it any time. The public freight market prices every load picked up here at them.
tower.amounts.h.freightPerKm: For every class of vehicle, empty run included.
tower.amounts.h.freightBaseFee: Paid once per load. A smaller vehicle starts from its share of it: a van half, a car a fifth, a motorcycle eight parts in a hundred.
tower.amounts.k.directPayFee: Our fee on a payment by Mollie
tower.amounts.h.directPayFee: Taken by Mollie from each payment a shipper makes straight to a carrier, for server costs, tax included. Empty: nothing is taken.
tower.amounts.directPayTitle: Paid straight to the carrier, by Mollie.
tower.amounts.directPayHint: Only where Mollie is how such payments are watched: the Netherlands. Each carrier gets one invoice a month for it.
tower.partner.owedNone: Nothing owed yet. Each step of a parcel carried under the partner’s promise shows here as it is done, at the partner’s own rates.
tower.partner.checks.title: Checks on the figures
tower.partner.checks.hintOpen: {n, plural, one {# to look at} other {# to look at}}
tower.partner.checks.lede: Fixed rules read what the partner owes every hour; once a day an AI review reads the week’s figures, shown tokens in place of names, phone numbers and ids. Each finding says why, in figures. Nothing here stops a step or holds a payout: mark a finding once you have looked.
tower.partner.checks.rule.never_held: Paid for a parcel it never held
tower.partner.checks.say.neverHeld: Paid for {reference}, which this hand never held.
tower.partner.checks.say.notOnRecord: Paid for {reference}, which is not on record.
